chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar said: He narrated to me Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Yaqoob ibn Yazid, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, who linked it up to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him).

He said: The one who enjoin to do good and admonish against evil is the one who possesses three characteristics: He acts according to what he orders, and abandons what he admonishes against; he is moderate in what he orders, moderate in what he admonishes, kind in what he orders, and kind in what he admonishes.
ai.seo_question: What are the three characteristics required to enjoin good and forbid evil in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq highlights that valid enjoining of good requires not only personal integrity but also a balanced temperament, ensuring that the guide is neither harsh nor permissive. This triad of practice, justice, and gentleness reflects the Shia emphasis on the moral qualifications of the *alim* or leader, distinguishing true authority from mere vocal criticism. It underscores that effective da'wah must be rooted in self-discipline and approachable wisdom.
